hypotheses.claim: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, the weakest regimes are tight capacity (12 instances, VBS mean 18.3908), size 100 (12), clustered (8) and eccentric depot (12) — all sharing the structure that a fail-early worst-savings ruin set gets stuck in a small neighbourhood. Hypothesis: a multiplicative gate on removal_savings (load-near-capacity gate + demand gate + route-distance gate) combined with a stagnation-driven rank exponent p(stagnation_ratio) in [1.0, 3.0] will lower mean tour length versus the current session SBS of 16.0504 (session_r0003) by >0.5% on the tight-capacity and size-100 subsets while not regressing the loose/depot-central subsets, because the load gate preferentially destroys near-capacity routes (the binding constraint in tight regimes) while the rising exponent injects diversity only when the incumbent is frozen.

next_search_advice.direction: Exploit the L3 ruin-recreate skeleton's single evolvable hook `score_ruin_nodes` and push toward stagnation-aware diversification: evolve a multiplicative-gated, rank-power removal priority whose exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) starts near 1.0 (pure worst-savings removal) and rises toward 2-3 only as stagnation_ratio grows, so the search behaves exploitatively on tight-capacity/size-100 instances (where capacity packing is scarce and every route-merging removal matters) but switches to broad-shouldered, relatedness-weighted ruin sets once R2R acceptance stalls on clustered / eccentric-depot instances. Keep the deterministic Regret-2 repair, intra_2opt and record-to-record acceptance intact, and keep tie-breaking free of global RNG so anytime behaviour stays monotone under the 500 ms deadline.
